chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Breastfeeding is one and twenty months; if it falls short, it is a wrong to the infant."
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed duration for breastfeeding in Shia jurisprudence and what is the consequence of stopping early?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing twenty-one months as the complete period of breastfeeding (*radāʿ*), distinguishing it from the minimum weaning age. The Imam’s note that early cessation constitutes 'injustice' (*jawr*) underscores the ethical and legal weight of fulfilling this duty, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding child custody and nursing rights.
